qti-assessment-test.title: American Academy of CME - Interprofessional Heart Failure & Antimicrobial Stewardship Vignettes (ACCME/ACPE/ANCC Demo)

qti-assessment-item.title: Coordinate interprofessional GDMT initiation and electrolyte safety monitoring in HFrEF.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Coordinate interprofessional GDMT initiation and electrolyte safety monitoring in HFrEF.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: A 67-year-old patient hospitalized for acute decompensated HFrEF (LVEF 30%) is euvolemic after intravenous loop diuresis, with blood pressure 108/68 mmHg, eGFR 44 mL/min/1.73m2, and serum potassium 4.6 mEq/L on carvedilol and sacubitril-valsartan. Prior to discharge, which collaborative plan best aligns with current heart failure guidelines?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Initiate an SGLT2 inhibitor and low-dose spironolactone prior to discharge, with clinical pharmacy medication reconciliation and a nursing/lab BMP check scheduled within 7 days.
Defer both SGLT2 inhibitor and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist initiation for 3 months until outpatient LVEF repeat echocardiography.
Discontinue sacubitril-valsartan immediately initiated on admission because baseline eGFR is below 60 mL/min/1.73m2.
Start high-dose spironolactone 50 mg daily plus oral potassium chloride supplementation at discharge without lab follow-up for 6 weeks.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. With eGFR > 30 mL/min/1.73m2 and potassium < 5.0 mEq/L in a hemodynamically stable euvolemic patient, completing four-pillar generic GDMT with early 7-day electrolyte and renal monitoring improves post-discharge survival and readmission outcomes.
Incorrect. Delaying in-hospital GDMT optimization substantially lowers long-term uptake and increases 30-to-90-day heart failure readmission risk.
Incorrect. Moderate chronic kidney disease (eGFR 44) is not a contraindication to sacubitril-valsartan when potassium and blood pressure remain stable.
Incorrect. Starting 50 mg daily with supplemental potassium at eGFR 44 and baseline K+ 4.6 creates severe hyperkalemia risk and violates early lab monitoring standards.

qti-assessment-item.title: Enforce ACCME Standards for Integrity and Independence in accredited CE item authoring.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Enforce ACCME Standards for Integrity and Independence in accredited CE item authoring.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: An AI drafting pipeline converts a cardiology symposium transcript into pre/post-test items. Which draft stem requires immediate editorial rejection under ACCME Standards for Integrity and Independence in Accredited Continuing Education?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: A stem referring exclusively to a single sponsor's proprietary brand name without generic pharmacologic naming or balanced class alternatives.
A patient vignette reporting eGFR, serum potassium, and generic drug class options across interprofessional care roles.
An item pairing a clinical guideline recommendation with explicit adverse-event monitoring thresholds.
A post-test item measuring nurse-pharmacist-physician discharge handoff coordination after intravenous-to-oral diuretic transition.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Accredited clinical education must use generic non-proprietary names whenever possible and avoid promotional framing favoring a commercial interest's branded agent.
Incorrect. Clinical laboratory values and generic pharmacologic classes meet ACCME content-validity and Moore's Level 4 competence standards.
Incorrect. Presenting balanced efficacy and safety monitoring criteria strengthens clinical validity.
Incorrect. Interprofessional transition-of-care vignettes directly support Joint Accreditation team-based competencies.

qti-assessment-item.title: Apply antimicrobial stewardship de-escalation in hospitalized community-acquired pneumonia.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Apply antimicrobial stewardship de-escalation in hospitalized community-acquired pneumonia.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: A 59-year-old non-ICU inpatient treated empirically with intravenous ceftriaxone and azithromycin for community-acquired pneumonia is afebrile for 36 hours, tolerating oral intake, with negative MRSA nasal PCR and respiratory/blood cultures growing penicillin-susceptible Streptococcus pneumoniae. What is the optimal stewardship team action?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: De-escalate to targeted oral amoxicillin therapy and align total antibiotic duration to 5 days given clinical stability.
Continue broad-spectrum intravenous ceftriaxone for a mandatory 14-day inpatient course despite clinical stability.
Add intravenous vancomycin empirically prior to discharge to prevent post-viral secondary infection.
Switch to oral fluoroquinolone monotherapy for 10 days to broaden gram-negative coverage.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Culture-directed IV-to-PO narrow-spectrum beta-lactam de-escalation with a 5-day total course in clinically stable patients reduces C. difficile and resistance risk.
Incorrect. Prolonged broad-spectrum IV therapy in uncomplicated, clinically stable pneumococcal CAP increases line complications and antimicrobial resistance without benefit.
Incorrect. Adding empiric anti-MRSA coverage with a negative MRSA screen and confirmed susceptible pathogen violates core stewardship principles.
Incorrect. Escalating to a fluoroquinolone when narrow-spectrum amoxicillin is active introduces avoidable tendon, CNS, and C. difficile toxicity.
